author: Lightweight model draft for Clara (technical writing) via Claudia Atlas <claudia.atlas@agents.arcadia.local>
title: Let coding agents request work and keep one execution order
purpose: Coding agents can describe a desired result in a standard request, and Arcadia turns accepted requests into governed work. Every accepted Action goes into one operator-owned order, so the next Action is always the first eligible one in that order.
serves: The Project outcome of the operator stating what should happen while Arcadia routes and orders the work.
done_when: The operator sees one complete queue with the next eligible Action first, and an accepted agent request appears in that queue with a traceable receipt.
reading_note: Draft: 7 of the 9 Actions are done. The live proof is blocked, and the question reconciler is still open.

actions.title: Define a standard request format for coding agents
actions.why: Lets a coding agent describe a desired result in one predictable form that Arcadia can check without guessing.
actions.done_when: A strict request is checked against the standard form with no model call, and a request with duplicate or unknown authority fields is rejected.

actions.title: Put every approved Action in one execution order
actions.why: Gives the operator one explicit order, so the question of what is next has one deterministic answer.
actions.done_when: Each approved, unfinished Action has exactly one queue position, and blocked or waiting Actions stay visible in order with the reason they are not eligible.

actions.title: Turn accepted requests into queued work
actions.why: Lets a request from a coding agent end as traceable, queued work without manual file or record editing.
actions.done_when: An accepted request yields one traceable proposal, and acceptance applies the exact previewed change in one step, including queue placement.

actions.title: Let the operator reorder the work queue
actions.why: Lets the operator change the order by moving items, instead of editing numeric priorities.
actions.done_when: The dashboard shows the selected next Action first and the full queue beneath it with eligibility reasons, and each move is previewed before it applies.

actions.title: Prove agents can manage and reprioritize real delivery
actions.why: Shows the whole flow on one real request before the operator relies on it for actual delivery.
actions.done_when: One real request from an agent and the operator becomes the correct proposed records, and the operator corrects at least one interpretation before accepting.

actions.title: Check the live queue and its summary message end to end
actions.why: Confirms the queue, dashboard, command line and chat summary all show the same result.
actions.done_when: The live queue shows one complete order, and an accepted request produces one receipt and one Discord message naming the next eligible Action.

actions.title: Let agents create and amend plans through requests
actions.why: Lets an agent add or change a plan's Actions without choosing file paths or Git steps.
actions.done_when: A strict request can create a complete draft Plan, and a request on an existing Plan can add or amend its Actions and reorder unfinished ones in one previewed change.

actions.title: Propose a specific change when a request names an existing item
actions.why: Avoids a vague generic decision when the request already names a Plan, Action or Decision.
actions.done_when: When a request names an existing Plan, Action or Decision, the preview proposes a specific change to it, with no guessed priority, date or ownership.

actions.title: Stop re-asking questions that are already answered
actions.why: Reduces repeat questions to the operator by matching them to answers already recorded in the documents.
actions.done_when: Each open question with a recorded answer is reported with its exact source, and nothing is closed unless the operator confirms it.
